newsitem.title: UK: Logica shares tumble after profits warning.
newsitem.headline: Logica shares tumble after profits warning.

text.p: Shares in Logica Plc fell sharply on Friday after the British software group said it expected profit performance for 1996/97 would be a "little below market expectations".
The company said in a statement that profits would be affected by the translation effect of a strong pound and by a slower than expected headcount growth in the UK.
By 1021 GMT, shares in Logica had tumbled 83p to stand at 767-1/2p.
Logica made the statement after briefing a group of analysts earlier on Friday.
It also said order intake in the current financial year had been strong and that it expected strong revenue and profits growth for the coming financial year.

"The translation of European results has been severely affected by the strength of sterling which has risen around 15 percent against the major European currencies over the previous year," said chief executive Martin Read.
Read said the company was encouraged by the 1996/97 order intake which it expected to be up 20 percent on a volume basis, excluding newly acquired Logica France.
The company made pre-tax profits for the year to June 30, 1996 of 24.7 million stg.
